correctness.rationale: Fourier zeros are roots of the coefficient cubic on \(\mu_N\). If all three roots are unimodular, Vieta gives \(e_2=e_3\overline{e_1}\), so equal coefficient moduli reduce to \(|e_1|=1\). After rotating one root to one, this is equivalent to \(2\cos d(\cos s+\cos d)=0\), forcing an antipodal pair; the converse follows immediately from roots \(\{u,-u,v\}\). Sampling that triple on \(\mu_N\) gives three zeros exactly when \(-1\in\mu_N\), and explicit choices realize every smaller listed count. A fresh symbolic replay independently verified the trigonometric factorization.
correctness.risk: The classification is specific to consecutive four-point support and common coefficient magnitude.

Neither inspected source states the equal-modulus cubic antipodal classification or its finite-root-of-unity parity consequence. The closest Resultary theorem for arbitrary four-sparse signals on prime cyclic groups covers only prime dimensions and support geometry, not all composite/even \(N\) or the cubic structural equivalence.

final_claim: For equal-magnitude nonzero coefficients on the consecutive support \(\{0,1,2,3\}\subset\mathbb Z_N\), the attainable Fourier-zero counts are exactly \(\{0,1,2\}\) for odd \(N\) and \(\{0,1,2,3\}\) for even \(N\); structurally, a cubic with four equal coefficient moduli has three unit-circle roots exactly when the root triple contains an antipodal pair.
limitations: Support exactly \(\{0,1,2,3\}\) and equal nonzero coefficient magnitudes.
